topic: Danny got back last night from a long weekend in Lisbon with Kasia. The airline lost his suitcase on the way out, he spent four days in clothes from the airport shop and a market stall, and he's wearing one of the shirts now. Jess has just noticed it.

T.speaker: Jess
T.line: Hang on, Danny. What is that? Has that got pineapples on it?

T.speaker: Rhi
T.line: Oh my God, it has.

T.speaker: Danny
T.line: They're not pineapples, they're, um, they're artichokes, and it was eleven euros from a man at the market, so I'd stop there.

T.speaker: Hugh
T.line: Artichokes. Course

T.speaker: Femi
T.line: Eleven euros. For that.

T.speaker: Sunny
T.line: And Kasia let you out in it?

T.speaker: Danny
T.line: Kasia chose it.

T.speaker: Jess
T.line: Kasia chose it? Oh, that's not a shirt then, that's a punishment. What did you do
T.full: Kasia chose it? Oh, that's not a shirt then, that's a punishment. What did you do in Lisbon?

T.speaker: Danny
T.line: Nothing! The airline lost my suitcase.

T.speaker: Femi
T.line: Hang on, so Kasia had her case the whole time, all her stuff, and she still went to the man and picked that one?

T.speaker: Danny
T.line: She said I looked relaxed.

T.speaker: Rhi
T.line: Oh, she's seeing

T.speaker: Sunny
T.line: No, it's so she can find you in crowds.

T.speaker: Hugh
T.line: Relaxed. Which bit's relaxed, Danny, the artichokes or the button that's given up halfway down?

T.speaker: Danny
T.line: Hugh, your belt is baler twine.

T.speaker: Hugh
T.line: It's held a gate shut
T.full: It's held a gate shut nine year.

T.speaker: Rhi
T.line: So who's minding the gate now?

T.speaker: Hugh
T.line: Will. He's got a bit of the old binder twine on it, so if there's bullocks in Tesco Saturday you'll know why.

T.speaker: Jess
T.line: Oh, I'd go. I'd stand by the yoghurts with my phone out, that's my whole weekend sorted.

T.speaker: Femi
T.line: Did the case ever turn up, Danny, or is this it now
T.full: Did the case ever turn up, Danny, or is this it now, artichokes till Christmas?

T.speaker: Danny
T.line: It's in Frankfurt. Having a lovely time.

T.speaker: Sunny
T.line: Wearing your good shirts, no doubt.

T.speaker: Rhi
T.line: Ironed, and all. I've been in your airing cupboard, Danny, you've got jeans in there with creases down the front.

T.speaker: Jess
T.line: No. Creases? In jeans? My grandad did that
T.full: No. Creases? In jeans? My grandad did that, he'd iron them on the kitchen table Sunday nights, Danny, you're basically ninety.

T.speaker: Sunny
T.line: Hang on, why was Rhi in it?

T.speaker: Rhi
T.line: His immersion packed up in March, didn't it. Kasia made me tea and he stood in the landing holding a torch
T.full: His immersion packed up in March, didn't it. Kasia made me tea and he stood in the landing holding a torch like he was helping.

T.speaker: Danny
T.line: I was holding it very well.

T.speaker: Rhi
T.line: You were not, you had it on the ceiling half the time. And I'm stood there, reaching past the tank, and there's trays of mushrooms on the slats, drying, all brown and curled up, and he goes, oh don't touch those, they're fine.

T.speaker: Sunny
T.line: Danny. Describe them to me.

T.speaker: Danny
T.line: Brown, quite small, the cap sort of, sort of turns up at the edges, from the wood behind the cricket club
T.full: Brown, quite small, the cap sort of, sort of turns up at the edges, from the wood behind the cricket club, and I've eaten hundreds.

T.speaker: Hugh
T.line: The wood behind the cricket club. That's where the whole second eleven goes for a wee at tea, Danny. Has done since about nineteen eighty.

backchannels.after: goes for a wee at tea

T.speaker: Jess
T.line: Oh no. No, no, so they're not dried, they're, they're pre-seasoned. You've been eating the second eleven, Danny.

T.speaker: Femi
T.line: I took the kids up that wood. Halloween, the, the torch walk thing. My youngest stopped dead and said it smells like a man in there. I told her it was foxes.

backchannels.after: smells like a man in there

T.speaker: Rhi
T.line: Oh no. No. I swim in the brook at the bottom of that wood, Sunday mornings, I put my face in it
T.full: Oh no. No. I swim in the brook at the bottom of that wood, Sunday mornings, I put my face in it, don't you look at me like that, Hugh.

T.speaker: Hugh
T.line: Not a word from me. Only that brook comes down through my bottom field first, Rhi, so you're getting the bullocks as well.

backchannels.after: so you're getting the bullocks as well

T.speaker: Jess
T.line: See, this is why you don't get a midlife hobby, Rhi. I've been on my sofa watching Love Island, nothing's weed on me.
